fact: the cartridge is on a 16-bit bus, 5, 5 and 8 cycles for 8, 16 and 32 bits; the 32K work RAM is on a 32-bit bus at 1 cycle for each
here: code written as ARM runs from the 32K work RAM, resident there or copied there or to the stack before it runs; what runs from the cartridge is Thumb
pieces: every piece whose form is resident, copied or built

fact: the fast RAM is 32K, and its last 256 bytes hold the stacks and the BIOS's pointers
here: the bookkeeping is small (one matrix level, 20 tasks, 32 queued writes), routines are copied into a heap slot only while they are needed, and wait moves the stack

section: ARM Opcodes: Multiply and Multiply-Accumulate (MUL, MLA)
fact: the multiply with a 64-bit product is an ARM instruction; Thumb has none
here: the 16.16 multiply is an ARM routine in fast RAM that Thumb code calls, in The Broken Seal through a macro that returns through ip

fact: the BIOS divides, takes square roots and arctangents; the processor has no divider
here: never called: the library has its own, and the compiler's division is the library's routines under the compiler's names

fact: the BIOS unpacks LZ77, Huffman and run-length data
here: never called: the cartridge's formats are the game's own, each with a decoder in assembly

fact: Halt stops the processor until an interrupt; Stop ends only on a keypad, cartridge or serial interrupt
here: wait halts in a loop until its own VBlank flag is set; sleep arms the keypad interrupt and stops

fact: the BIOS saves r0 to r3, r12 and lr and jumps to the ARM routine whose address is at 03007FFCh
here: the handler is ARM, resident in fast RAM, and saves r4 itself, since the routines it calls destroy it

fact: a channel is a source, a destination and a control word, twelve bytes; a transfer starts at once, at VBlank or at every HBlank
here: Dma_Set writes the three with one instruction; HBlank transfers feed a register a new value each line

fact: the layer's reference point is copied at VBlank and stepped each line; written during the frame it sets the current line
here: the World Map gives every line its own terms, computed by an ARM routine copied to RAM

section: GBA Sound Channel A and B - DMA Sound
fact: two sample queues fed by DMA at a timer's rate; mixing voices into them is the program's work
here: a mixer in fast RAM, part Nintendo's driver and part Camelot's own

fact: the ROM begins with an ARM branch to the program
here: the header and the start-up code are assembly, ARM
